meta.tagline: Research, field notes, and plain-language briefings on the state of AI in South Carolina.
meta.mission: The SCAiL Institute studies how artificial intelligence is landing in real South Carolina communities — who it helps, who it leaves behind, and what closes the gap — and publishes what we learn for free.

reports.title: The State of AI in South Carolina 2026
reports.summary: Our inaugural annual report: a county-by-county look at AI readiness, workforce exposure, education access, and economic opportunity across all 46 counties.

articles.title: Three Things Every SC Small Business Should Do With AI This Quarter
articles.excerpt: You don't need a data team. You need one afternoon and these three moves — drafting, summarizing, and customer follow-up — to get real leverage from tools you already have access to.
articles.author: SCAiL Institute

articles.title: The Quiet Workforce Shift Happening in the Upstate
articles.excerpt: Manufacturing and logistics anchor the Upstate economy. Here's how AI-assisted tooling is changing what a good job looks like there — and what training has to catch up.
articles.author: SCAiL Institute

articles.title: AI Literacy Is the New Financial Literacy
articles.excerpt: A generation ago, not understanding compound interest cost families their future. Today, not understanding AI does the same thing. Here's the parallel — and the fix.
articles.author: Joshua German

articles.title: What Grant Funders Get Wrong About Rural AI Programs
articles.excerpt: Well-meaning funding often assumes urban infrastructure and urban problems. A note to funders on what actually moves the needle in South Carolina's rural counties.
articles.author: SCAiL Institute

articles.title: A Glossary of AI Terms, Explained Like You're at the Kitchen Table
articles.excerpt: Model, token, hallucination, agent, prompt. Twenty AI terms defined without a single equation — the reference we hand out at every community class.

articles.title: Why We Started with Literacy Instead of Jobs
articles.excerpt: Everyone wants to talk about AI jobs. We think that's step two. Here's the case for teaching a whole community to understand AI before we try to place anyone in it.
